name: Origin Private File System
plain: A private, fast file area per site that the person cannot browse and that counts against quota.
meaning: Hosts SQLite or media caches in the browser. Invisible to the person in the file manager, uses the origin quota, and lasts until site data is cleared. Needs no prompt, unlike the File System Access picker.

access.persistence: Same lifetime and quota as other origin storage
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

limits.headline: Can keep fast private files in the browser that count against its storage limit
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the app saves large files, databases or offline data.
can: Store files in a private browser area
cannot: Show them in your file manager
Keep more than the site's storage limit

story.what_it_is: A private, fast file area per site that you cannot browse and that counts against your storage space.

marketing.name: Origin Private File System
marketing.pitch: Google pitches it as fast, private file storage in the browser for databases and big files.

story.for_you: You never see it. It is why some web apps handle big files fast, and why a site can take up storage you cannot find in a folder.
story.for_makers: It gives web apps quick, real file access with no prompt. Makers use it for in browser databases, big media and offline tools. It counts toward the quota the browser sets for each site.

use_cases.example: A browser game keeps its big world files and saves here for fast loading.
A web video editor keeps your clips here while you cut them.
A browser database like SQLite keeps its data file here.
A note or document app keeps its offline library here.
A web music or podcast app keeps downloaded episodes here.
A hidden ID file here is not shown in any normal browser storage list.

technical_bounds: Sync access handles only in dedicated workers
No access to the real file system

legit_uses: Large local databases (SQLite WASM), game assets

history.change: Shipped in Safari with worker sync access
